Article Title: HCLTech jumps over 7%, TCS up 5%: Why are IT stocks rallying
Article Text:
IT stocks jump 5%

Why are IT stocks rallying?

Inflation, crude prices remain top concerns

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

Dalal Street began Tuesday on a strong note, with tech-heavy stocks fuelling the gains and pushing the BSE Focused IT index and Nifty IT around 3% higher. HCLTech emerged as the top gainer, rising 7.11% to 1306.80 after reporting strong quarterly results a day earlier, backed by improved profitability metrics.Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest IT company, also gained 5.69% to 2248.00 after announcing a 15% rise in net profit in its quarterly earnings last week. Other IT stocks joined the rally, with Tech Mahindra climbing 3.52% to Rs 1,521.70 and Infosys rising 2.06% to Rs 1,038.Around 10:55 am, the Nifty IT index was up 3.12%, or 885.65 points, at 29,235.25, while the BSE Focused IT index had gained 3.04%, or 1,044.37 points, to 35,366.87. The broader market also traded higher, with BSE Sensex rising 466.15 points, or 0.65%, to 72,390.83. Nifty 50 was up 145.30 points, or 0.65%, at 22,508.65.Better-than-expected quarterly results from major IT companies have encouraged investors to return to beaten-down shares, raising hopes that concerns over the sector's earnings growth may be easing.Dharmesh Kant, head of equity research at Cholamandalam Securities, told Reuters, "The quarterly numbers reported by Accenture, TCS, and HCLTech indicate that the worst of earnings growth concerns for IT companies might be behind us.This is triggering a value buying opportunity in the sector."Despite Tuesday's rally, IT stocks have had a difficult year.The Nifty IT index has fallen 23% year-to-date amid moderating earnings growth and concerns about artificial intelligence disrupting traditional software services businesses.Rupee's recovery provided further support to market sentiment. The currency strengthened to 95.25 against the dollar after the Reserve Bank of India announced additional measures to ease pressure on the domestic currency.Investors are also keeping a close watch on the interest rate outlook after retail inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 5.54% in September. The latest reading has put the Reserve Bank of India's rate decisions in focus.Crude oil prices remain another concern. Brent crude futures fell by more than 1% during the day but continued to trade above $100 per barrel. Persistently high oil prices have fuelled inflation worries, particularly amid a weak monsoon.While domestic IT stocks advanced, global technology shares faced pressure following reports of rapid technological advances by Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies.The developments triggered a global sell-off in chipmakers, with South Korea's technology-heavy Kospi falling 6%. An index tracking Asian shares excluding Japan declined by more than 2%.
Article Summary: HCLTech emerged as the top gainer, rising 7.11% to 1306.80. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest IT company, also gained 5.69% to 2248.00. Despite Tuesday's rally, IT stocks have had a difficult year.

Article Title: Gold price prediction today: Will gold trade cautiously? Check October 14, 2026 outlook
Article Text:
A soft CPI or a dovish tone from Warsh could take gold towards $4,220-4,310.

Gold price prediction

today:

Gold prices are likely to trade cautiously with no clear catalyst for a big rise, says Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst - Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers.

Below is her outlook:

Gold: Focus This Week and the Next

Gold Price Outlook

Technical Levels

Gold (Spot) CMP: $4,161/oz

Support: $4,070 / $4,000

Resistance: $4,220 / $4,310

MCX Gold CMP: Rs 1,48,300

Support: Rs 1,45,050/ Rs 1,42,700

Resistance: Rs 1,50,400/ Rs 1,53,400

Silver:

International Silver CMP: $59.21/oz

Support: $58 / $57

Resistance: $62/ $65

MCX Silver CMP: Rs 2,18,800

Support: Rs 2,14,300/ Rs 2,10,600

Resistance: Rs 2,29,000 / Rs 2,40,200

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold has had a cautious week, recovering from a low of $4,066.54 last Wednesday to close at $4,194.24, up 1.28% for the week. This week the rebound has stalled, with spot trading around $4,160 after briefly crossing $4,200 on Monday.Silver is stuck near $59-60 after failing to hold above $61. The dollar index is near an 18-month high of 102.20 and the US 10-year yield is above 5%, both of which continue to weigh on bullion. Brent near $105 keeps inflation fears alive, and markets still see about an 85-90% chance of a Fed hike in December, against only 17% for October.The comments from the New York Fed’s Williams, who sees one more hike this year but none in 2027, helped yields ease a little, but not enough to spark a real recovery. In India, MCX gold ended last week at Rs 1,51,499 per 10 gm, but has slipped about 1.1% to near Rs 1,49,860 this week as the rupee rallied sharply after the RBI’s measures.What stands out is how strongly investors are still buying despite the headwinds.Global gold ETFs took in about $10 billion in September (67.3 tonnes) and a record $31 billion in the third quarter, taking total holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes. North American funds saw their first quarterly inflow of 2026, and UK funds had their strongest quarter on record. Yet the physical market tells a different story.Bank of America notes that central banks, China and India have slowed their buying, and that weak prices could eventually prompt ETF holders to sell.The big event is today’s US September CPI, the last inflation reading before the Fed meets, followed by producer prices and import prices later in the week. On Thursday, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at the IMF annual meeting in Bangkok, and the market will look for hints on the pace of tightening.Markets will also watch oil and Hormuz headlines, and whether the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire is confirmed, since Ukraine says no deal is finalised. For Indian markets, the rupee remains a second driver of MCX prices as it has turned volatile and strengthened after RBI’s recent measure.Looking ahead to next week, attention shifts to the Fed meeting on 27-28 October, where officials such as Cleveland’s Hammack and Dallas’s Logan want more than one additional hike, while Williams does not.The near-term picture stays cautious. Gold lacks a clear catalyst for a sustained turnaround, and rallies are likely to meet profit-taking as yields and the dollar stay high. A soft CPI or a dovish tone from Warsh could take gold towards $4,220-4,310, while a hot print or hawkish surprise could pressure prices back towards support at $4,070-4,000.Bank of America expects gold to average $4,000 in the fourth quarter, with a possible low of $3,750, and says it needs a more dovish Fed or renewed debasement fears to turn higher. Until then, ETF investors and central banks should continue to offer a floor, but gains are likely to remain capped.
Article Summary: Gold prices likely to trade cautiously with no clear catalyst for a big rise, says Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst - Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers. A soft CPI or a dovish tone from Warsh could take gold towards $4,220-4,310.

Article Title: RBI’s ‘bazooka’ sees rupee rising 1.4% versus dollar in two days, but should central bank let it fall?
Article Text:
A currency is said to be undervalued when it is weaker than what experts believe is its fair value.

RBI’s measures

These measures were:

RBI's Rupee Defence: 4 Key Measures

How long will the effect last?

Brent Crude Price Trend Line

FPI outflows

Should RBI let the rupee depreciate?

What RBI governor said on rupee

Where is the rupee headed? The Indian currency has been in a free fall for several quarters now. At one time its one-year forward even breached the 100 mark prompting experts and economists to wonder if the rupee will cross the 100 mark versus the US dollar.A lot has changed since then. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has stepped in to build a record foreign exchange reserves chest to arm itself with tools to intervene in the forex market. The FCNR(B) deposits scheme helped attract billions of dollars, putting India in a comfortable position on the forex reserves front.Yet continued capital outflows, high oil prices, uncertainty on the US-Iran war front, and rising US bond yields have added pressure to the currency, pushing it to record lows of almost 97.More recently, RBI’s measures unveiled last week have led to the rupee appreciating sharply. On Friday it closed at 96.61. Since then it has appreciated by Re 1.36 or 1.41% to 95.24.One thought process is that the RBI should allow the market forces to let the rupee find its levels. Indeed the IMF recently said that India should allow the exchange rate to act as a shock absorber.Interestingly, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra believes that the rupee is actually undervalued.A currency is said to be undervalued when it is weaker than what experts believe is its fair value based on underlying economic fundamentals.However, an undervalued currency does not automatically mean it will strengthen soon. The currency can continue to remain weak for an extended period because of capital outflows, global uncertainty or other market pressures.What should RBI do? How effective would its latest measures be for long-term prospects of rupee? And, should the rupee be allowed to depreciate?Last week, RBI unveiled what SBI Research has called a bazooka to protect the rupee’s slide.RBI opened a direct dollar-supply window for three state-run OMCs shifting roughly $10-12 billion per month away from the open spot market.The daily CRR maintenance has been raised to 99% and simultaneously to tighten liquidity in the system the RBI has announced a Rs 25,000 crore OMO sales.RBI has tightened foreign exchange derivative regulations by prohibiting the rebooking of cancelled rupee derivative contractsIt has lowered the threshold for taking FX derivative positions without underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million across all Authorised DealersIt has strengthened documentation requirements to prevent duplicate hedging, and introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve for larger contracts.Vivek Kumar, Economist at QuantEco sees RBI’s special measures as a comprehensive package for addressing both internal and external macro pressures.“The dual focus on increasing the price of money (i.e., interest rate) and restricting its availability (i.e., draining surplus liquidity) is an appropriate policy response to the emerging inflation and currency risks,” Vivek Kumar tells TOI.In addition, tighter regulation of rupee hedging and trading will dramatically shrink space for speculation and short-circuit the self-fulfilling expectation of currency weakness.The effect may however be short-term.Interest rate increases by the US Federal Reserve have historically put emerging markets under pressure through shifts in capital flows, financing conditions and exchange rates.The Federal Reserve raised rates on September 17, marking its first increase since July 2023.As Vivek Kumar points out: the underlying pressure on the rupee from a firm dollar, elevated energy prices, and continued portfolio outflows persists.“As such, while these measures will help to stabilise the rupee, they won't engineer a reversal beyond the initial knee-jerk relief rally. Since the rupee remains exposed to the current set of adverse global factors, durable stability will be conceivable only if the global tensions ease,” he says.“Meanwhile, the RBI could focus on maintaining an ex-ante real policy rate of 1.0-1.5% to ensure durable macroeconomic balance. This can be complemented with measures to attract foreign investment,” he adds.Yet another important factor is the central bank’s stance that it will not target any particular level of the rupee versus dollar. Any intervention will be aimed at curbing speculative pressures and volatility.Ranen Banerjee of PwC India says that the recent measures taken by RBI will surely address the pressures on rupee caused by speculative trades.“These measures are not towards addressing the fundamentals of demand and supply of forex but more to make the supply more orderly for the oil companies and make the demand for forex real and not speculative,” he explains.SBI Research says that while the RBI has been taking all possible steps to thwart a seemingly difficult global playbook, there is an urgent need also by the government to address some of the long pending structural issues regarding capital inflows. For example, it recommends abolishing the long-term capital gains tax on equities. This would help deal with capital outflows more effectively.There are the costs associated with a weaker rupee.While exports benefit from a depreciating currency, imports become costlier. In the current scenario, with oil prices high, it acts as a double whammy when India imports higher inflation.And, the inflationary pressures for a net importing country like India increase with a weaker rupee. The fiscal pressures also increase owing to higher energy and fertiliser costs in rupee terms.Sujan Hajra, Chief Economist at Anand Rathi Group notes that the immediate costs are especially relevant for India, whose crude-oil import dependence reached approximately 88.7% in FY2025–26, according to PPAC data.“Depreciation compounds an oil-price shock, raising domestic production costs and potentially inflation. It also increases the rupee burden of unhedged foreign-currency debt, reduces purchasing power and can weaken foreign investors’ dollar returns. Crucially, depreciation raises the rupee cost of imports immediately; improvement in the dollar trade balance requires a subsequent response in export and import volumes,” he explains.Hence, experts say the aim should be to have the exchange rate closer to the real effective exchange rate and not target a particular exchange rate.Radhika Rao, Senior Economist and Executive Director at DBS Bank cautions against the fallout of letting rupee depreciate.“While exchange-rate flexibility is a shock absorber, policymakers will be mindful of the risk that one-way currency depreciation can become self-reinforcing. Preventing a disorderly depreciation is therefore as important as preserving flexibility,” she tells TOI.“Beyond a point, it can become destabilsing for capital flows, price stability and sentiments, requiring an active policy response,” she adds.Rao is of the view that the breadth of the restrictions highlight the authorities view that the USD/INR is nearing a defacto red line and that the recent bout of rupee depreciation is being viewed as disorderly rather than fundamentals driven.Ranen Banerjee, Partner and Leader, Economic Advisory at PwC India says that the rupee should find its natural level based on the dollar forex demand and supply.“Targeting an exchange rate is always futile as we have only limited firepower and means to address external factors that determine forex flows. Volatility owing to speculation on the rupee needs to be managed and that is what RBI is doing,” he tells TOI.As Sujan Hajra points out: A record low against the dollar does not, by itself, establish whether the rupee is cheap or expensive.“Valuation requires examining inflation-adjusted exchange rates against trading partners, productivity and the external balance. Equally, a fundamentally undervalued currency can weaken temporarily when dollar demand exceeds supply,” he tells TOI.“I favour calibrated intervention to prevent self-reinforcing depreciation, alongside sufficient flexibility to accommodate persistent external pressures. The objective should be orderly adjustment and anchored inflation expectations,” he says.Economists believe that the economy’s growth momentum, demand in the Indian economy and the opportunities for growth are being currently overshadowed by capital flows to AI centred investments, higher yields in the developed markets and higher oil prices.“It is a cycle and we need to manage the macro through this cycle as there has been no change in the underlying fundamentals of the Indian economy as can be seen from the growth forecasts being upgraded by almost all external agencies,” Banerjee says.IMF may favour market-driven exchange rate adjustments, but for RBI orderly currency movements assume priority.And, as the RBI governor pointed out, the rupee is undervalued, which means the economy’s fundamentals do not warrant such sharp levels of depreciation.DK Srivastava, Chief Policy Advisor at EY India says the US dollar remains overvalued and the rupee undervalued.“Rising US bond yields are attracting capital flows into the US, including from India, adding pressure on the rupee and deepening its undervaluation,” he tells TOI.“In this environment, the RBI should continue to guide the rupee along a trend consistent with inflation differentials. While inflation remains elevated in both economies, India’s CPI inflation averaged 4.8% during June-September 2026, compared with about 3.4% in the US during June-August 2026, suggesting that some depreciation may be warranted,” Srivastava adds.
Article Summary: The Indian currency has been in a free fall for several quarters now. At one time its one-year forward even breached the 100 mark. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has stepped in to build a record foreign exchange reserves chest to arm itself with tools to intervene.

Article Title: India's economic story in fast lane, IMF projects 7% GDP growth for FY27 and FY28
Article Text:
India's growth story remains strong

India holds its ground despite higher oil prices

World Bank, OECD raise India growth forecasts

Global growth faces a more fragile outlook

India’s economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), keeping the country among the fastest-growing major economies despite growing uncertainties. According to the institution, strong domestic demand, robust services activity and favourable demographic trends are expected to support this growth.India's growth prospects were supported by favourable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms, even as higher oil prices posed a challenge.“India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favorable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms.”The forecast comes amid a series of upgrades by global agencies after India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter of the current financial year.The agency expects India to remain among the fastest-growing major economies, with domestic demand and services activity helping sustain momentum.“India remains among the fastest-growing major economies, with growth in 2026 projected at 7.0 percent.This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity.”It also highlighted how the Indian economy continued to expand despite rising oil prices. “India’s growth remained robust, underpinned by domestic demand and services, despite higher oil prices.”The improved outlook follows the stronger-than-expected GDP growth recorded in the April-June quarter, prompting several global institutions, including the World Bank, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), S&P Global Ratings, Moody's Ratings, Fitch Ratings and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to raise their growth estimates for India.The World Bank raised its growth projection for India in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.6% estimated earlier. The multilateral agency attributed the revision to strong domestic demand and exports, despite global headwinds. It expects the economy to grow by 7.2% in 2027-28.The OECD has also increased its forecast for India's GDP growth in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.3% projected in June. The revised estimate is higher than the 7% forecasts from S&P, Moody's and ADB, while Fitch expects growth of 6.9%.Moody's Ratings raised its forecast for India's real GDP growth in FY27 to 7%, from 6%, citing the economy's resilience amid the Middle East conflict."Although we continue to expect India to grow faster than all other G-20 economies, as well as similarly rated emerging market sovereigns, risks remain," Moody’s said.Expansion in the April-June quarter was supported by strong investment and manufacturing activity, which helped offset weakness in mining and consumer-facing services.While India has received a series of growth upgrades, the IMF has warned that the global economy's resilience is becoming increasingly fragile and uneven.“The global economy remains resilient, but that resilience is becoming more fragile and more uneven. Growth is projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, while inflation is expected to reach 4.7%, driven largely by higher energy and food prices.”The global outlook also presents risks for India.Higher crude oil and energy prices could fuel inflation and put pressure on household purchasing power. Below-normal monsoon rainfall could affect agricultural output and rural demand, while prolonged geopolitical tensions could disrupt supply chains and increase input costs.Despite the upward revisions to India's growth projections, these factors remain among the risks flagged by agencies assessing the country's economic outlook.
Article Summary: India's economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027. Strong domestic demand, robust services activity and favourable demographic trends are expected to support this growth. The IMF has warned that the global economy's resilience is becoming increasingly fragile and uneven.

Article Title: From Chinese money laundering to Russia, Iran sanctions - why was Bank of America fined $1.21 billion?
Article Text:
File photo: US Treasury Department announced a $1.2 billion fine against Bank of America for violating anti-money laundering laws

Violated Bank Secrecy Act

Bank of America has been fined $1.21 billion by US regulators for failing to detect and report billions of dollars in suspicious transactions, including activity linked to potential money laundering and sanctions violations.The US treasury department said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious activity, including $1 billion that posed national security-related and other illicit finance risks. The unreported activity included transactions that may have involved Chinese money laundering networks and trade-based laundering linked to the US southwest border, according to the Treasury.The department said the bank prioritised revenue while building its compliance programmes and relied too heavily on inquiries from law enforcement and other financial institutions rather than its own internal controls. This effectively outsourced a substantial part of its responsibility to proactively detect and report suspicious activity, it said.As part of the settlement, Bank of America admitted that it had “willfully violated” the Bank Secrecy Act by failing to maintain a compliant anti-money laundering programme, conduct required due diligence on foreign correspondent accounts and file suspicious activity reports, the Treasury said.The $1.21 billion penalty includes a $750 million civil fine imposed by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the largest in the regulator’s history. The OCC said the bank had failed to address shortcomings in its anti-money laundering programmes identified in a 2024 cease-and-desist order. It described the bank’s compliance programme as “deficient and ineffective” and said its transaction monitoring system had delayed reports covering billions of dollars in transactions.The bank also agreed to pay $11.6 million to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) over 475 apparent violations of sanctions programmes targeting Russia, Iran, narcotics and global terrorism. OFAC said the settlement reflected its determination that the apparent violations were “non-egregious”.Under the settlement, the bank must hire an independent third party to review past transactions, identify suspicious activity it failed to detect and report those transactions to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).Bank of America said it had invested billions of dollars in technology and dedicated thousands of employees to fighting financial crime. It added that it was committed to completing the work required by regulators and had already devoted substantial personnel and resources to remediation.The bank said its third-quarter results, due on Wednesday, would include a non-tax-deductible charge of $1.2 billion, reducing net income by approximately 17 cents per share.The penalty comes days after American Express was fined $350 million for similar anti-money laundering shortcomings. Bank of America shares fell 2.7% in after-hours trading on Tuesday, after closing down 1.1%.
Article Summary: Bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious activity, including $1 billion that posed national security-related and other illicit finance risks. The $1.21 billion penalty includes a $750 million civil fine imposed by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

Article Title: Woman applied for 130 IPO shares, bank entered only 65; consumer commission awards Rs 37,000 for deficient service but rejects her Rs 40 lakh compensation claim
Article Text:
The commission rejected her demand for Rs 40 lakh in compensation, describing the amount as “highly excessive”. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission provide some relief?

Rs 20,000 for deficiency in service.

Rs 10,000 for mental agony and harassment.

Rs 7,000 towards the costs of the original proceedings and the present appeal.

You apply for a certain number of shares for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) and then discover that the bank has recorded only half of the number! What do you do in such a case where there is a cut in the potential size of your allotment?This is what a woman, an Ahmedabad resident, faced. She claimed the bank's mistake caused her a loss of Rs 42,142 and sought a compensation of Rs 40 lakh.In 2022, the woman applied for 130 shares in an IPO. However, the bank recorded her application for just 65 shares, which she claimed resulted in a loss of Rs 42,142. She also accused the bank of causing her physical and mental harassment.Also Read | Rs 5.89 crore FD interest slashed from 7.75% to 3.5% without notice; Delhi High Court rejects bank’s non-renewal argument and orders interest at an average of earlier rates The woman initially took her complaint to the Ahmedabad District Consumer Commission, but her appeal was dismissed. She subsequently approached the Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. The state commission heard the matter and ruled in her favour, though it granted her only partial relief.The woman claimed that the discrepancy resulted from an error by the bank, which, according to her, acknowledged the mistake in an official communication.Representing his wife, her husband argued that the bank could not escape responsibility by dismissing the mistake as “typographical” or “clerical”. He also submitted that her account had sufficient funds to cover the IPO application.Had the bank entered the correct number of shares, he argued, she would have been allotted 130 shares.“A data-entry or clerical error committed by a bank employee, if it results in financial loss to the customer or deprives the customer of a financial benefit, cannot be treated as an ordinary or significant mistake,” her counsel argued according to an ET report, citing ICICI Bank vs Santosh Sardana (2021).The bank’s counsel argued that the transaction was intended to facilitate an investment in shares with the objective of earning a profit. On that basis, the lawyer maintained that it was a commercial activity and the woman did not meet the definition of a ‘consumer’.“Share trading is a commercial activity and an investor is not a “consumer” within the meaning of the Consumer Protection Act”, the bank’s counsel said.Also Read | She worked as a teacher till 62 years of age instead of retiring at 60, but was denied gratuity because of extended service; Allahabad HC orders payment with 6% interest The bank's lawyer also contended that the Ahmedabad District Consumer Commission was right to conclude that the woman had not furnished proof of payment of consideration to the bank. According to the counsel, she had also failed to provide documentary evidence showing that she was entitled to an allotment of 130 shares and had lost that entitlement because of the bank's alleged mistake.The District Commission rejected her complaint on the ground that she did not qualify as a consumer. It held that investing in shares amounted to a commercial activity and, consequently, the complaint was not maintainable, Supriya Majumdar, Partner at Elarra Law Offices, told ET.The Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission subsequently partly allowed the woman’s appeal.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing parties After considering the arguments from both sides, the Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission held that the woman could be considered a beneficiary of the bank's services. It said that the fact that she had not directly paid the bank did not, by itself, conclusively establish that she was not a consumer.The commission also observed that a transaction involving shares does not automatically make every dispute concerning banking services associated with an IPO a commercial dispute. Therefore, the woman could not be denied the right to seek redressal against the bank merely because her complaint arose from an IPO application.“Banking institutions are required to maintain a reasonable degree of care, accuracy, and diligence when processing applications and entering customer-related information,” the commission stated according to the ET report.However, the commission did not agree with the woman’s claim that she had suffered a loss of Rs 42,142. It also rejected her demand for Rs 40 lakh in compensation, describing the amount as “highly excessive”.Instead, the commission directed the bank to pay her:The total amount payable to the woman was therefore Rs 37,000.Supriya Majumdar said the woman succeeded in her appeal on two counts: the maintainability of her complaint and the deficiency in the services provided by the bank.During the appeal, the complainant also submitted a SEBI circular to argue that banks providing IPO-related services were entitled to receive charges or compensation from another institution or entity.“Thus, although the complainant may not have personally paid any consideration to the bank, the circular indicated that the IPO-related service was not necessarily a service rendered entirely without consideration, as the bank was entitled to receive compensation,” she explained.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claims The commission rejected the claimed financial loss because allotment in an IPO is governed by prescribed procedures and subscription ratios. Consequently, assuming that the woman would certainly have received all 130 shares was speculative.Majumdar emphasised that, although the bank had admitted entering an incorrect number of shares in the application, the woman had not established that the error caused her a loss of Rs 42,142.Her claim depended on the “assumption” that she would necessarily have been allotted 130 shares had the application been recorded correctly, rather than on concrete evidence demonstrating that outcome.For this reason, the commission declined to award the Rs 40 lakh compensation she had sought.Also Read | Man paid Rs 1.73 crore for Gurgaon flat, waited over a decade without possession; builder alleges homebuyer bought it for commercial gain, consumer commission awards refund with 12% interest & Rs 4 lakh
Article Summary: An Ahmedabad resident applied for 130 shares in an IPO in 2022. The bank recorded her application for just 65 shares, which she claimed resulted in a loss of Rs 42,142. She also accused the bank of causing her physical and mental harassment. The woman initially took her complaint to the Ahmedabad District Consumer Commission.

Article Title: Man jointly bought Rs 80 lakh property with father and wife but didn't file ITR; taxman added Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained money, but ITAT grants relief after proof of family contributions
Article Text:
The bench examined the additional evidence submitted by the man, including banking records and documents. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT delete the tax additions ?

Significance of ruling

A man bought a residential property along with his wife and father. However, he did not file his income tax return for the year.The tax department opened his case for reassessment and adding Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained investment. The Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) deleted the Rs 55.2 lakh addition made to a taxpayer's income. Here’s what the case is about:A man bought a residential property jointly with his wife and his father. The Income Tax Department reopened his assessment for the 2016-17 assessment year after receiving information through its Risk Management Strategy that he had purchased an immovable property during the 2015-16 financial year. The assessment proceedings recorded that he had not filed an income tax return for the relevant year.Also Read | Wife sold shares for Rs 8.31 crore LTCG, bought husband’s Mumbai property for Rs 7.5 crore and claimed Section 54F exemption; taxman calls it tax avoidance, but ITAT Mumbai gives relief to her During reassessment, the man explained that the property had been funded through several sources, including a Rs 32 lakh housing loan from a bank and contributions from himself and his family members. The assessing officer accepted the housing loan but considered that the remaining investment was insufficiently explained.The officer calculated the addition using total payments of Rs 87.2 lakh and deducted the accepted housing loan of Rs 32 lakh, treating the balance of Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained investment under Section 69 of the Income Tax Act, read with Section 115BBE.The National Faceless Appeal Centre upheld the addition. It found that the evidence submitted at that stage did not adequately establish the sources of the contributions attributed to the man’s father and wife.The man then approached the ITAT, challenging both the addition and the calculation underlying it. He argued that the property was jointly owned and that the payments had come from identifiable sources. He also disputed the assessing officer’s use of Rs 87.2 lakh, contending that the actual payments, including VAT, were Rs 84 lakh.Before the tribunal, the man submitted additional documents, including bank statements, employment and remuneration records, and material relating to his father’s pension and funds.Also Read | Delhi couple repaid Rs 1.41 crore home loan, but the bank lost their original sale deed property papers; consumer commission orders Rs 15 lakh compensation plus Rs 50,000 costs The bench examined the additional evidence submitted by the man, including banking records and documents concerning the family members’ financial contributions.It found that the payments towards the property could be identified and were supported by documentary material. The evidence also established that the property had been purchased jointly, rather than solely by the man.According to the judgement, the assessee explained the sources towards the acquisition as a housing loan of Rs 32,00,000/-, contribution by his father of Rs 11,20,000/-, contribution by his wife of Rs 20,00,000/-, his own funds of Rs 1,70,000/- and further funds of Rs 19,10,000/-.The tribunal considered the housing loan, the taxpayer’s own funds and the contributions attributed to his wife and father in the context of the records placed before it.The significance of the additional evidence was that it addressed the gaps in the explanation that the lower authorities had relied on when making and sustaining the addition.Also Read | Son claimed share in mother’s Delhi house, saying he paid Rs 1.5 lakh for land and Rs 60,000 for construction; Delhi High Court rejects claim, orders him and wife to vacate The calculation of the investment was another important issue. The agreed consideration recorded for the property was Rs 80 lakh. The man contended that actual payments, including VAT, were Rs 84 lakh, while the assessing officer had used Rs 87.2 lakh to calculate the unexplained investment.The tribunal found that the higher figure adopted by the assessing officer was not substantiated by the documents on record. The discrepancy mattered because the Rs 55.2 lakh addition had been calculated by deducting the accepted housing loan from the higher payment figure.The tribunal held that the investment could not be treated as unexplained in the manner adopted by the assessing officer.The tribunal therefore deleted the Rs 55.2 lakh addition under Section 69 read with Section 115BBE.According to Raghav Bajaj, Partner at Khaitan & Co, the ruling restates an important principle: Section 69 is not a tool for presumptive attribution.Before an investment can be taxed as unexplained, it must first be established that the taxpayer has made an investment, and only then ask whether its source has been satisfactorily explained.The immovable property was bought jointly by a son, his father and his wife. It was financed through a joint housing loan and paid for through traceable bank transfers from each of their accounts.“Despite this, the entire balance was attributed to one co-owner by the tax officer. The Tribunal held that an addition built on assumption, and on numbers that cannot be reconciled with the actual payments evidenced by documents, is not valid,” Bajaj explains.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claim The decision matters well beyond its facts. Pooling salaries, pensions, savings and inherited funds to buy a home is a familiar reality for Indian families, and this ruling recognises each such contributor's role, Bajaj tells TOI.At the same time, the case is a cautionary tale – taxpayers should keep a clear, person-wise record of contributions from the day of purchase in similar facts.“Further, it must also be noted that analytics-led reassessments are a legitimate and efficient way to identify high-value transactions, but a data flag is the beginning of an inquiry, not its conclusion. Where title is shared, each co-owner's sources must be examined on their own merits, and any addition must be confined to the share genuinely left unexplained,” Bajaj adds.However, according to him, one significant question remains open. The taxpayer also challenged the validity of the reopening itself, arguing that the income that could have escaped assessment did not exceed the Rs 50 lakh threshold relevant to the limitation provisions.“Having decided the case on merits, the Tribunal did not rule on that point. Taxpayers facing similar reassessments should therefore raise and preserve jurisdictional challenges from the outset, alongside a well-documented defence on merits,” he says.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or sale
Article Summary: A man bought a residential property along with his wife and father. However, he did not file his income tax return for the year. The tax department opened his case for reassessment and added Rs 55.2 lakh as unexplained investment. The Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) deleted the addition.

Article Title: ‘Ahead of Starlink in queue’: Sunil Mittal would be happy if Eutelsat OneWeb gets nod ‘at least a few days’ before Elon Musk’s satellite communications venture
Article Text:
Sunil Mittal said the company's ground network had been ready for three years, while its satellites had been hovering over India for five years.

‘Will be happy to get nod at least few days before him’

Amid the controversy surrounding Elon Musk-owned Starlink’s India entry, Bharti Airtel Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal on Wednesday said his satellite communications venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, had applied for a licence in India five years ago. According to Mittal, Eutelsat OneWeb was well ahead of Elon Musk 's Starlink in the queue.The statement comes after Musk recently claimed on X that certain oligarchs were preventing Starlink from entering the Indian market because they wanted to retain a "monopolistic chokehold" on Indians. Musk posted another question on X, asking whether Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani was "the real boss of India."The Ministry of Communications has rejected the allegation that India's regulatory framework or its implementation was unfair or discriminatory and described such suggestions as "baseless and misconceived".Mittal said that he would be pleased if his company received approval even a few days before the US tech billionaire's venture.Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, Mittal said: "I think I am significantly ahead in the queue from him. I applied five years back." His remarks came in response to a question about Musk's recent criticism of India's telecom billionaires amid the ongoing debate over satellite internet services in the country.Mittal said the company's ground network had been ready for three years, while its satellites had been hovering over India for five years.Despite this, Eutelsat OneWeb is still awaiting permission to launch its services in the country. "We don't have the permission, so we'll be very happy to get it at least a few days before him," Mittal said.Last week, Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia had reiterated that monopolies were not permitted in any sector in India."Let me set the record straight. For us, the Department of Telecommunications, we are technology agnostic... Our job is to be able to provide the bouquet of services to every single customer. It is for the customer to choose in a free market which service he or she prefers, and within that service bouquet, which company's service he or she prefers," the minister had said during a briefing at the recent India Mobile Congress.Scindia said three companies had already obtained satellite communications licences: Musk's Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb. Amazon's Project Kuiper has also expressed interest in the Indian market but will have to follow the prescribed procedure.The minister noted that while much of the discussion had focused on one particular company, three entities had already secured satcom licences."We are very clear on our stand. There are three parties that have got a licence; as and when the government decides the charge system on the revenue basis, that spectrum will be assigned to them, and as and when they individually fulfil the security conditions, they can start operations," the minister had said.Scindia also informed that the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) and the Department of Telecommunications were nearing a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication spectrum.
Article Summary: Bharti Airtel Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said his satellite communications venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, had applied for a licence in India five years ago. The statement comes after Musk recently claimed on X that certain oligarchs were preventing Starlink from entering the Indian market because they wanted to retain a "monopolistic chokehold"

Article Title: KL University and KLH Hyderabad campuses enter the agentic AI era
Article Text:
​KL University and KLH Hyderabad campuses enter the agentic AI era

Note (*): The claim has been verified against the MoU provided by the

KONERU LAKSHMAIAH EDUCATION FOUNDATION

.

Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

Artificial intelligence is moving beyond chatbots and content generation, with autonomous systems increasingly capable of reasoning, planning and executing tasks. KL Deemed to be University and KLH Hyderabad are bringing this next phase of AI into higher education through a new partnership with HCL Group AI Labs, with its Agentic AI Campus initiative taking shape across its academic ecosystem, including its Vaddeswaram and Hyderabad campuses.The initiative, also unveiled at KLH Hyderabad, will integrate AI and agentic technologies into academic programmes, laboratories, projects and day-to-day learning, with AI-focused degrees also planned.The partnership is built around a broader shift in how students engage with technology. Rather than limiting AI to a standalone subject, the university plans to embed it across disciplines and enable students to progress from using AI tools to designing and deploying intelligent systems.Students will be introduced to machine learning, generative AI, large language models and agentic architectures, alongside practical capabilities such as prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, multimodal applications, intelligent chatbots, AI copilots, enterprise assistants, intelligent search and decision-support systems.The curriculum will also connect these emerging capabilities with core software skills, including programming, full-stack development, cloud computing, databases, DevOps and application deployment. This combination is intended to help students understand not only how AI systems work, but also how to build, integrate and operate them in real-world environments.“AI is transforming how industries operate, innovate and create value, and universities must embed it across the learning ecosystem rather than treat it as a single subject,” said Koneru Satyanarayana, Chancellor, KL Deemed to be University. “Working with HCL AI Labs, we want students across disciplines to move from using AI tools to designing,” he adds.According to Srinath, Dean – Student Skilling and Progression, the programme will use project-based learning to translate classroom concepts into working applications. Students will tackle use cases spanning healthcare, education, agriculture, manufacturing, finance, retail, cybersecurity, smart cities, human resources and enterprise automation.Industry-led problem statements, hackathons and product competitions will add practical exposure, with promising ideas encouraged towards startups and market-ready solutions.The programme will cover the complete development journey, from identifying a problem and preparing data to building, testing, deploying and refining an AI solution. The university expects this approach to prepare graduates for emerging roles such as AI engineers, agentic AI developers, generative AI engineers, machine learning engineers and AI product engineers.
Article Summary: KL University and KLH Hyderabad campuses enter the agentic AI era. The initiative will integrate AI and agentic technologies into academic programmes, laboratories, projects and day-to-day learning. Students will tackle use cases spanning healthcare, education, agriculture, manufacturing, finance, cybersecurity, smart cities and enterprise automation.

Article Title: Why Gen Z needs a different approach to education
Article Text:
.

Measure learning through capability

Recognise the individual learner

.

Teach students to think with technology

Develop initiative and global capability

Prepare students to keep learning

This article has been contributed by Dr. Amol Gawande,

Director of Brookstone Institute of Global Studies, Dubai, and an Executive Board Member of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS)

Disclaimer: The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

For generations, education followed a predictable path. Learn what is taught, complete a degree, find a job and build a career. But Gen Z is entering a world where artificial intelligence, automation and evolving skill requirements are reshaping that journey.I believe education must respond by combining strong academic foundations with the ability to apply knowledge in unfamiliar situations.Information is available almost instantly. Students can access lectures, research and practical demonstrations from across the world. The greater educational challenge is helping them interpret that information, question assumptions and use it well. My experience in management education has reinforced a simple principle: students need opportunities to apply, experiment, reflect and improve throughout their studies.Completing a syllabus does not necessarily mean a student can analyse a business problem, communicate an idea or lead a team. We need to judge education by the capabilities students develop, alongside the knowledge they acquire.Outcome-based education provides a framework for this shift. It asks what students should be able to demonstrate after a course, then connects teaching and assessment to those outcomes. In management education, these may include analytical thinking, financial understanding, communication and effective teamwork.I have emphasised internships, corporate interaction and project-based learning throughout my academic leadership. Case studies, simulations and live projects give concepts a practical context. They also allow students to encounter problems without a single textbook answer. Academic rigour becomes more meaningful when students can use it to explain a decision or develop a solution.Students bring different strengths, interests and ambitions to the classroom. Some are drawn to entrepreneurship; others excel in analysis or communication. Many need support in identifying a career direction.Personalised learning does not require a separate curriculum for every student. It requires attention to the individual behind the qualification. Mentoring, career counselling, psychometric assessment and development tailored to a student’s profile can help them understand their strengths and make informed choices. Education should help students explore the professionals they could become, as well as the degrees they can complete.Adding AI or robotics to a curriculum is only a starting point. Students also need to understand how technology affects business models, professional decisions and careers.When a tool generates an answer, the learner must still judge whether the question was useful, the answer is sound and the application is appropriate. Critical thinking, creativity, communication and ethical reasoning therefore belong at the centre of technology education.My experience increasingly intersect with digital transformation and emerging technologies. That experience reinforces my view that technical familiarity must be accompanied by judgement. Students need to understand how to think with technology and use it responsibly.Entrepreneurship education extends beyond starting a company. It develops the habit of identifying problems, testing solutions, accepting uncertainty and creating value. I have advocated for students to become creators of opportunities. That mindset is equally useful within an established organisation, where an employee may spot a problem and develop a better way of working.Global exposure also needs a clear educational purpose. Travel alone cannot create global competence. Students need opportunities to understand different markets, cultures and ways of thinking through exchanges, international collaborations and cross-cultural projects.In my academic leadership experience, international partnerships have created opportunities for student and faculty exchanges, joint programmes and collaborative research. Their educational value lies in helping participants work across differences and apply what they learn in a globally connected environment.A graduate’s first job may not define their eventual career. As industries and roles evolve, the knowledge gained at the beginning of working life will need to be revisited. Education must develop the confidence and habits to learn, unlearn and relearn.This requires classrooms that remain connected to the world outside them. Real business problems, industry interaction and opportunities to experiment should be part of the learning experience. Strong conceptual knowledge provides the foundation; practical experience helps students test and deepen their understanding.I believe educators must ask whether our education systems are ready for the students we teach. Our responsibility is to develop people who can think independently, apply knowledge and continue learning long after graduation. For Gen Z, that is the educational experience we need to build.
Article Summary: For generations, education followed a predictable path. Learn what is taught, complete a degree, find a job and build a career. But Gen Z is entering a world where artificial intelligence, automation and evolving skill requirements are reshaping that journey. Education must respond by combining strong academic foundations with the ability to apply knowledge in unfamiliar situations.

Article Title: Rollout of BS-VII in 3 phases from April 2029 to April 2035
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Govt is all set to roll out BS-VII emission standards, aligned with Euro 7 norms, in phases, starting April 2029. The new norms will set stricter limits on harmful pollutants, including nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulate matter amid heightened pollution risks across Indian cities.BS-VII will start with new cars and SUVs manufactured from April 2029, followed by small goods delivery and pick-up vans from 2030 and buses and heavy-duty vehicles from April 2031. The new norms for two-wheelers - the biggest contributor to pollution - will, however, be notified later.Unlike BS-VI, which was first rolled out from April 2020, it will not require changes in the refinery infrastructure to produce petrol and diesel suitable for the upgraded emission standards, officials said. It will, however, require the automobile sector to upgrade engines.TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry has approved the proposed timeline, and draft notifications for the three categories of vehicles are expected over the next few days. The proposed emission norms will not affect existing vehicles or their life, including those compliant with BS-VI standards.The proposed standards will strengthen emissions monitoring beyond controlled laboratory tests to ensure vehicles comply with prescribed limits under real-world driving conditions and throughout their operational life.The implementation of all the new norms will be in three phases spanning six years - April 2029 to April 2035 - giving adequate time to industry and testing agencies.According to the finalised norms, the cut-off limits of various emission components for cars and SUVs remain unchanged compared with BS-VI. Particulate number has, however, been reduced fr-om 23 nanometres to 10 nanometres, resulting in improved filtration of pollutants. Smaller particles penetrate deeper into lungs. A person aware of the matter said the proposed change makes the regulation more stringent by capturing ultrafine particles, which have been unregulated thus far.The transition from BS-VI to BS-VII will have more impact on trucks and heavy-duty vehicles, with the proposed standard aimed at reducing emissions in the range of 20-50% across pollutants. This will be more stringent for on-road emissions.People involved in framing the norms said BS-VII goes beyond tailpipe emission by regulating non-exhaust sources such as brake wear and tyre abrasion. Moreover, the new norms will introduce the concept of market surveillance, where independent testing agencies will conduct in-use compliance checks.Officials said the norms are fully aligned with Euro 7 and its implementation, which was also structured in a phased manner, starting Nov 2026 for light-duty vehicles and May 2028 for heavy-duty vehicles. The full rollout will extend up to 2035.
Article Summary: BS-VII will start with new cars and SUVs manufactured from April 2029. It will be followed by small goods delivery and pick-up vans from 2030. The new norms for two-wheelers - the biggest contributor to pollution - will, however, be notified later.

Article Title: Apple makes fresh push into smart homes market
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Apple is making a renewed push into the smart home market, unveiling three new devices - HomeView, HomePod mini 2 and Apple TV 4K - as it looks to take its newly launched Siri AI beyond smartphones and establish a stronger presence in connected homes. The launches mark Apple's latest attempt to challenge Amazon and Google in a market where it has struggled to gain significant traction despite its strong presence in premium consumer electronics.The centrepiece of the announcement is HomeView, a smart home display that acts as a central hub for controlling connected devices, managing household activities and interacting with Siri AI. The device is priced at Rs 39,900.Apple also introduced the second-generation HomePod mini at Rs 18,900 and a refreshed Apple TV 4K, starting at Rs 39,900. The new devices will become available in phases, beginning Oct 30."Apple must demonstrate that context-aware AI makes the connected home meaningfully more useful, while addressing interoperability and adoption barriers," said Prabhu Ram, VP, industry research group, CyberMedia Research (CMR).
Article Summary: HomeView is a smart home display that acts as a central hub for controlling connected devices. Apple also introduced the second-generation HomePod mini at Rs 18,900 and a refreshed Apple TV 4K, starting at Rs 39,900. The new devices will become available in phases, beginning Oct 30.

Article Title: IMF raises India growth forecast to 7%
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has upgraded India's growth forecast for the current year to 7%, from 6.4%, making it the fastest-growing major economy.The agency joins others - including the World Bank, ADB, S&P and Moody's - in upgrading its projections after official data estimated first-quarter growth at 7.8%. Most global agencies have forecast 6.9-7% growth in the current fiscal year. IMF's latest World Economic Outlook estimated inflation at 5% this year with per capita output projected to rise 4.7% in 2026 compared with 5.2% last year.It said that the global economy, projected to grow 3.4% in 2026, has stayed resilient despite multiple shocks in recent years. "India remains among the fastest-growing major economies, with growth in 2026 projected at 7%. This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity," the multilateral agency said.India along with Germany has seen the highest revision, with Saudi Arabia forecast to contract 3.3% this year, seeing a five-percentage-point cut in the projection."India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favorable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms," IMF said.The report highlighted efforts to diversify trade flows and pointed to India's trade deals with the UK and the European Union that will lower tariffs and reduce barriers to services trade, and "facilitate adjustments to recent trade policy changes". US tariff actions have resulted in a flurry of trade deals across the globe, with India too moving ahead with FTAs that have been on the negotiating table for years.
Article Summary: IMF has upgraded India's growth forecast for the current year to 7%, from 6.4%, making it the fastest-growing major economy. Most global agencies have forecast 6.9-7% growth in the current fiscal year. IMF's latest World Economic Outlook estimated inflation at 5% this year.

Article Title: Now, MDR on UPI to be rolled out after Diwali
Article Text: MUMBAI: Amid pushback from industry, National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has deferred the rollout of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions until after Diwali. In a statement on Tuesday, NPCI said that a new date of implementation will be notified separately. The merchant fee was earlier supposed to come into effect from Oct 15, amid the peak Navratri season when festive sales volumes surge.Retailers heaved a sigh of relief as the move will spare them the need to reconfigure billing and accounting systems, besides briefing store staff at the point of peak footfalls."Deferment avoids this and gives the trade time to prepare.....the festive quarter is the single most important trading window for apparel retail. UPI has become the default payment mode at the store counter, and any change in the cost of accepting it directly affects checkout practices, reconciliation and consumer experience," said Santosh Katariya, president, Clothing Manufacturers Association of India (CMAI).Payment companies recovered from early losses after NPCI confirmed that MDR implementation would begin immediately after Diwali.Paytm fell over 7% to Rs 1,571 before recovering 9.1% to close at Rs 1,714, up 1.5%. One MobiKwik Systems recovered from a 4% dip to close at Rs 245, up 1.7%, while Pine Labs rebounded from Rs 154.4 to Rs 164.8, gaining 1.1%.Associations, however, urged govt to revisit the Rs 2,000 threshold given that a large share of apparel retail value (particularly for purchases made during weddings and festive) breaches that mark.The MDR framework was approved by NPCI on Sept 15, with a 0.4% charge for eligible person-to-merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above.Kumar Rajagopalan, executive director & CEO at Retailers Association of India (RAI), said that the fee should ideally be a fixed amount rather than a percentage of the transaction value. He added that inflation has already been squeezing their margins.
Article Summary: NPCI has deferred the rollout of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions until after Diwali. The merchant fee was earlier supposed to come into effect from Oct 15. Retailers heaved a sigh of relief as the move will spare them the need to reconfigure billing and accounting systems.

Article Title: How phones on EMI are driving loan demand for two-wheelers
Article Text: MUMBAI: Consumer durable loans, such as those for buying a mobile phone on EMI, are helping lenders build credit histories for younger borrowers, contributing to a decline in two-wheeler loan delinquencies to a seven-year low of 1.4% in June 2026 from 2.7% in June 2019, according to TransUnion Cibil.First-time borrowers accounted for 39% of two-wheeler loan originations in the first half of 2026, down 19 percentage points from pre-pandemic levels. Meanwhile, 43% of borrowers had more than two years of formal credit history, up from 27% in 2019. Another 18% had less than two years of credit history, indicating more than 60% of borrowers had an established credit record, according to TU Cibil's latest report, Shifting Gears 2026: Credit Drives Today's Mobility.Consumption-led borrowing has contributed to this shift. Nearly a third of two-wheeler borrowers had consumption credit products in their credit histories in the first half of 2026, up from 22% in the corresponding period of 2019. Consumer durable loans featured in the histories of 18% of borrowers and gold loans in 16%, credit cards in 12% and agriculture-related credit products in 8%.NBFCs held 73% of outstanding two-wheeler loans.
Article Summary: First-time borrowers accounted for 39% of two-wheeler loan originations in the first half of 2026. 43% of borrowers had more than two years of formal credit history, up from 27% in 2019. NBFCs held 73% of outstanding two- wheeler loans.

Article Title: Zoho pauses hikes and ad spend due to rising AI costs
Article Text: CHENNAI: Zoho has paused hikes for its employees and is cutting down marketing spend due to inflation, rising AI-related expenses and challenging geopolitical and market conditions, said the company's founder and chief scientist, Sridhar Vembu. In a post on X on Tuesday, he wrote that AI usage has driven up costs significantly amid a challenging geopolitical environment. He added that the company will work hard to avoid mass layoffs. "We have cut down on our marketing budget. We have also told our employees that we cannot have our usual pay increase this year. I have apologised for not being able to avoid this," Vembu said. TNN
Article Summary: Zoho has paused hikes for its employees and is cutting down marketing spend due to inflation, rising AI-related expenses and challenging geopolitical and market conditions. "We have cut down on our marketing budget. We have also told our employees that we cannot have our usual pay increase this year," Vembu said.

Article Title: Who is Neha Bora? From Delhi University to JNU, the education and activism of AISA’s president
Article Text:
Who is Neha Bora? Know about her education, PhD research and journey from theatre to student politics

Educational journey from Delhi University to JNU

Theatre and the beginning of activism

The 23-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar

Recent protests and detention in Delhi

Neha Bora, the 29-year-old national president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA), has drawn national attention for her participation in student-led protests, including a recent demonstration in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A doctoral scholar at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), Bora combines academic research in theatre and performance studies with political activism. Her recent detention after a dash towards Connaught Place, following an agitation called near RK Ashram Marg Metro station, brought her activities into the public spotlight.Born in Khatima, Uttarakhand, Bora grew up moving between cities because her father served in the Indian Army. She completed her schooling in Bengal, where she encountered the writings and political ideas of Charu Majumdar, Pablo Neruda and Arundhati Roy.Bora graduated in sociology from Hindu College, University of Delhi, before pursuing postgraduate studies at Dr B. R. Ambedkar University. She subsequently joined JNU’s School of Arts and Aesthetics for a PhD in theatre and performance studies.Bora’s involvement in public causes developed through theatre.During her time at Delhi University, she participated in plays addressing social issues and later became associated with Sangwari, a Delhi-based street theatre group. She has described her transition from theatre to politics as an organic progression.The 2019 protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act also influenced her political engagement. She later joined AISA, a Left-wing student organisation associated with the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation, and became its national president.Bora joined fellow student leaders Manish Kumar and Aameen Amitoj in a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar alongside activist Sonam Wangchuk. The three continued their fast for 23 days before ending it on July 20 following appeals from MPs, activists and public figures. Reports said Bora lost eight kilograms during the protest.The agitation highlighted opposition to the National Education Policy, 2020 and the centralisation of competitive examinations, issues she says have fuelled student concerns for years.On Sunday, October 11, Bora led supporters towards Connaught Place after police action around the protest gathering. She announced their arrival on social media at 2.51pm and was detained shortly afterwards.In a video posted on X, she alleged that protesters faced cramped conditions and mistreatment inside a police bus. Police had not responded to these allegations in the reports available.Bora also participated in protests in Jharkhand, where ink was thrown at her near the state Assembly on August 7. Her speeches have attracted controversy, including police complaints over remarks concerning Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
Article Summary: Neha Bora is the national president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) She has drawn national attention for her participation in student-led protests. A doctoral scholar at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Bora combines academic research in theatre and performance studies with political activism.

Article Title: 'Making progress': Taiwan on Alaska LNG deal after Trump says it will buy 30% of output
Article Text:
Taiwan advances Alaska LNG deal.

Taiwan said on Wednesday it was making progress in negotiations to buy liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Alaska and planned to invest up to $4.4 billion in the project. The announcement came after US President Donald Trump said Taiwan had agreed to buy 30% of the proposed project's output.Taiwan's economy ministry said state-owned energy company CPC Corp had made significant progress with the project developer after nearly 18 months of negotiations and evaluation.Under the plan, CPC would purchase 6 million metric tonnes of LNG annually once production begins, in line with a letter of intent signed last year.The company would also participate in the project's development, with an estimated investment of up to $4.4 billion, the ministry said, Reuters reported."Specific investment arrangements, equity stakes and related terms will be determined through subsequent negotiations and commercial contract procedures," it added.However, the final investment terms and purchase commitments remain subject to further negotiations and commercial agreements.Taiwan has been looking to increase purchases of US natural gas and reduce its dependence on other suppliers. Earlier in February, officials said US gas would account for about one-third of the island's imported supply this year.The proposed Alaska LNG project is designed to export up to 20 million metric tonnes of LNG annually. The project has been discussed for decades, but its commercial viability remains a concern for some industry experts.If completed, the pipeline would provide a direct route for US LNG to Asian markets, including Taiwan, without requiring shipments to pass through the Panama Canal or travel around the Horn of Africa. This could reduce shipping times and costs.The move is also part of Taiwan's effort to narrow its large trade surplus with the United States, which has angered the Trump administration.CPC signed an agreement with the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation last year to buy LNG and invest in the project. Alaska's governor said in March 2025 that Taiwan had signed a letter of intent to purchase 6 million metric tonnes annually.Taiwan President Lai Ching-te had said the investment would help strengthen the island's energy security.Last year, Taiwan Presidential Office Secretary-General Pan Men-an also visited the proposed project site in Alaska as the Trump administration promoted the project to Asian allies.Trump at a rally in Alaska on Tuesday said that Taiwan had agreed to buy 30% of the project's output.US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who attended the event organised by the Republican National Committee, said Taiwan had committed $4.4 billion towards the pipeline's development.Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai, responding to Trump's remarks said the government's responsibility was to "stabilize the entire energy supply and build its resilience, like governments everywhere."The announcement did not establish whether a final, binding agreement had been signed. Taiwan's economy ministry said the investment arrangements and equity stakes would be settled through further negotiations.Last month, Trump said South Korea had agreed to invest in the Alaska LNG project, which he valued at $54 billion. Seoul, however, said the proposed investment had not yet been finalised.
Article Summary: Taiwan says it is making progress in negotiations to buy liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Alaska. Announcement came after US President Donald Trump said Taiwan had agreed to buy 30% of the proposed project's output. Taiwan has been looking to increase purchases of US natural gas and reduce its dependence on other suppliers.

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Title: Wall Street mixed as bank earnings lift Goldman, Iran war and inflation weigh
Article Text:
The S&P 500 fell 0.1 per cent, the Dow Jones dropped 190 points or 0.4 per cent, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.2 per cent.

Trading revenue supports bank earnings

Wall Street stocks traded mixed on Tuesday as investors assessed a fresh batch of corporate earnings, with strong results from major US banks offset by concerns over market volatility, inflation and the economic fallout of the Iran war.The S&P 500 slipped 0.1 per cent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 190 points, or 0.4 per cent, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.2 per cent. The moves came as the benchmark indexes remained close to their record levels, with investors weighing whether companies can sustain their profit growth amid rising borrowing costs and geopolitical uncertainty.Goldman Sachs shares recovered to trade 0.3 per cent higher after initially jumping more than 4 per cent following a stronger-than-expected quarterly profit. The bank benefited from robust equities trading, although revenue from its fixed income, currencies and commodities business fell 1 per cent from a year earlier.Chief executive David Solomon said the economy remained resilient despite several headwinds. "The economy continues to be very, very resilient despite some of the headwinds," he said, pointing to a strong technology investment cycle and a regulatory environment encouraging corporate activity.Banking activity faces late-quarter slowdownResults from JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo indicated that the dealmaking and trading momentum seen in the first half of the year may have moderated towards the end of the third quarter. Executives cited volatile equity markets, rising bond yields and uncertainty surrounding the economic outlook as factors weighing on investment banking activity.JPMorgan said market turbulence had slowed dealmaking and affected bond trading, particularly during the second half of September. However, chief financial officer Jeremy Barnum said the pipeline of potential deals remained "very strong", with many transactions delayed rather than cancelled.Goldman Sachs chief Solomon also expressed optimism about future activity, saying the initial public offering (IPO) market remained in good shape despite a recent loss of momentum. Companies could postpone listings until market conditions improve, he said.Citigroup chief financial officer Gonzalo Luchetti reported softer investment banking activity during the quarter, while Wells Fargo finance chief Mike Santomassimo also pointed to a slowdown in September as benchmark bond yields rose sharply."There is no doubt that high interest rates and the threat of continued Fed hikes is weighing on trading and IB activity in a measurably negative vector," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management.Equities trading remained a bright spot for major banks as clients adjusted their portfolios amid uncertainty over interest rates and rising energy prices.
